g.text: Validating Germany's hand-mapped OpenStreetMap tier against MaStR

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #c9bda4

g.text: Germany's register is complete by law, so it can say what a mapped polygon is really worth. (1) Measured on the polygons containing exactly one

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #c9bda4

g.text: registered unit, the rooftop constant falls from 0.200 kWp/m² on small features, which are genuinely arrays, to 0.051 on large ones, which outline

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #c9bda4

g.text: roofs and sites. (2) Almost all the mapped area sits in that largest band, so a flat 0.18 turned 8.8 GWp into 22.0. (3) Ground-mount needed no

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #c9bda4

g.text: constant change, but 300 km² of polygons above 5 km² contain no registered unit at all, and registration is mandatory.
